einzeiler: Osama bin Laden's descent from Saudi elite to stateless fugitive in Sudan and Afghanistan
kurzfassung: This episode traces Osama bin Laden's journey from his post-Soviet war celebrity in Saudi Arabia to his exile in Sudan. Joined by guest Steve Coll, the hosts examine bin Laden's opposition to the US military presence in the kingdom, his funding of militant networks, and mounting international pressure that eventually forced his move to Afghanistan. The discussion details how his escalating attacks and anti-regime rhetoric led to his loss of Saudi citizenship and family ties.
stichpunkte: Osama bin Laden returned to Saudi Arabia in 1989 as a celebrated veteran of the Soviet-Afghan war.
Following Saddam Hussein's invasion of Kuwait in 1990, bin Laden opposed the deployment of Western troops in the kingdom and offered his own militia instead.
Rejected by the Saudi royal family and allied with conservative preachers, he began openly denouncing the regime and the US military presence.
Under growing pressure and facing restrictions on his passport, bin Laden relocated to Sudan in 1992, establishing businesses and an international militant network.
During his years in Khartoum, he funded various operations and associated himself with attacks in Yemen and East Africa, though his direct command varied.
Discontent grew as the US and Saudi governments tracked his financial and operational links to incidents like the 1993 World Trade Center bombing.
Under severe international pressure, Sudan expelled bin Laden in 1996, leading to the dismantling of his family compound and his return to Afghanistan.
Upon arriving in Afghanistan, bin Laden secured an alliance with the Taliban leader Mullah Muhammad Omar, opening a new chapter for his organization.

clips.hook: Why the Saudi royal family rejected bin Laden's offer
clips.text: The royal family dismissed his military proposal because they had already committed to a massive international defense coalition, making a reversal politically humiliating.

clips.hook: The happiest years of Osama bin Laden's life
clips.text: His time in Khartoum offered domestic stability, horse farms, family life, and the freedom to expand his revolutionary organization and communicate internationally.

clips.hook: A defector walks into a US embassy with inside information
clips.text: An operative who embezzled funds fled to Eritrea and provided American diplomats with detailed operational intelligence about the inner workings of the network.

clips.hook: The 1993 World Trade Center bombing details
clips.text: A rented van carrying half a ton of explosives detonated in the basement parking garage, killing six people and injuring over a thousand.

clips.hook: A deadly car bomb in Riyadh rattles the Saudi regime
clips.text: An explosion destroyed a military training facility and killed five Americans, creating an acute crisis for the kingdom and its foreign alliance.

beschreibung:
How did the Gulf War drive a permanent wedge between Osama bin Laden and the Saudi royal family? Why did the bin Laden family finally decide to disown him? How did he manage a global terror network from a farm in Sudan?

In Episode 4 of this series, William and Anita are joined by Pulitzer Prize winner Steve Coll, author of The Bin Ladens: An Arab Family in the American Century, to follow Osama bin Laden’s descent from the Saudi establishment into international exile.
